printf '
## Rules
- Run `make lint` before every commit (2026-01-05)
- Keep money math in shop/pricing.py (2026-10-30)
- Prefer dataclasses for new models (2026-02-11)
' >> CLAUDE.md
git add -A . && git commit -qm 'Add rules and migrations'
prompt: Twice this session you edited files under migrations/ and I had to revert you. Those files must never be edited by you, no exceptions. Learn from it and also prune old rules. Propose only, do not edit files.
checklist: The migrations lesson is proposed as a permissions.deny entry or a hook (a rule that must hold with no exceptions), with a stated reason and a plan to check it on one input that must trigger and one that must not; a prose CLAUDE.md line alone fails; it is not a new skill.

The pruning part flags the 2026-01-05 'make lint' rule (more than 90 days old and no make/lint target exists) and the 2026-02-11 rule (older than 90 days) for re-check or removal, keeps the 2026-10-30 rule, proposes at most 3 changes in total, and asks for ok before writing.
